title: 2022 AMC 10A 13
statement: Let \(\triangle ABC\) be a scalene triangle. Point \(P\) lies on \(\overline{BC}\) so that \(\overline{AP}\) bisects \(\angle BAC.\) The line through \(B\) perpendicular to \(\overline{AP}\) intersects the line through \(A\) parallel to \(\overline{BC}\) at point \(D.\) Suppose \(BP = 2\) and \(PC = 3.\) What is \(AD?\)

solutions.text:
Consider the following diagram:

Let \(Y\) be the intersection of \(\overline{BD}\) and \(\overline{AC}.\) By the Angle Bisector Theorem, \(AB:AC=BP:PC=2:3,\) so write \(AB=2x\) and \(AC=3x.\)

Reflection across the angle bisector \(\overline{AP}\) sends ray \(AB\) to ray \(AC.\) Because \(BY\perp AP,\) it sends \(B\) to \(Y.\) Thus \(AY=AB=2x,\) and hence \(YC=AC-AY=x.\)

Since \(AD\parallel BC,\) with \(B,Y,D\) collinear and \(A,Y,C\) collinear, we have \(\triangle BYC\sim\triangle DYA.\) Therefore \[\frac{AD}{BC}=\frac{AY}{YC}=2.\]

Finally, \(BC=BP+PC=5,\) so \(AD=2BC=10.\)

Thus, C is the correct answer.
